raw.details:
Overview: Celestia is a 24hr Open Innovation hackathon organised by HyprLAN at Rajarajeswari College of Engineering, Bangalore. Teams pick a real problem, build a working solution within the event window, and present it to a panel of industry professionals and faculty. It is open-ended: any domain and any idea is welcome, as long as it is original and works.

Join the community: Community Link

Event Details:

  • Dates: 5th and 6th November 2026

  • Venue: Rajarajeswari College of Engineering, Bangalore

  • Registration: 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM on 5th November

  • Inauguration: 10:15 to 11:00 AM

  • Hackathon: 11:00 AM on 5th November to 10:00 AM on 6th November

  • Mid-event judging: A judging round every six hours during the hackathon

  • Final judging: 10:00 to 11:00 AM on 6th November

  • Prize distribution: 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM

  • Judges: Three industry professionals and two internal judges

  • Team size: 2 to 4 members

  • Prizes: ₹20,000 for the winner, ₹10,000 for the runner-up and ₹5,000 for third place

Eligibility: The hackathon is open to everyone, from the tech field or the non-tech field. The only requirement is that every participant is registered and verified on Unstop.

Phases of the Hackathon

  • Phase 1, Online Round: Teams register on Unstop and submit their idea as a PPT. The submissions are evaluated, and qualifying teams move to Phase 2.

  • Phase 2, Offline Round: Qualified teams come to the venue and build their solution overnight. They face judging rounds every six hours, then final judging and the prize distribution.

Rules and Regulations:

  • Each team must have 2 to 4 members. All members must be registered, and a participant may be part of only one team.

  • All work must be the team’s own. Existing libraries, frameworks, APIs, open source tools and public datasets are allowed. Copied work will result in disqualification.

  • Any hardware that poses a safety risk is prohibited.

  • Participants must wear their ID cards at all times.

  • Any damage to college property, including glass, will be the responsibility of the team concerned.

Judging Criteria:

Projects will be judged on impact, creativity, originality, technical implementation, feasibility and presentation.

Registration Process:

  • Register on Unstop.

  • Submit your idea as a PPT on Unstop before the deadline.

  • Submissions will be evaluated, and qualifying teams will be informed that they move to the next round.

  • Qualified teams pay the registration fee: ₹450 per team for the first 10 teams, and ₹500 per team after that.

  • Teams then come to the venue and take part in the hackathon.

Important Instructions:

  • Jury Sessions: Three jury sessions will be held after the hackathon begins, one every six hours. Teams must be prepared to explain their progress at each session.

  • Submission: Before the announced deadline, each team must submit a working prototype, a source code repository or link, a project description, a PPT with documentation, and a video of the working project.

  • Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, cables and additional devices, along with hardware components (if needed). Only internet access will be provided by the organisers.

  • Hardware: All hardware must be functional and demonstrable during the final evaluation.

  • Movement: Participants are requested to stay within their assigned desks, floors and rooms, and to be accompanied by a volunteer when stepping out. For security reasons, participants are requested to remain on campus after 9:00 PM and until the prize distribution is concluded, unless there is an emergency.

  • Meals: Breakfast, lunch and dinner must be taken only within the time slots allotted to the teams.

  • Belongings: Participants are fully responsible for their own belongings. The organisers will assist in locating lost items where possible but accept no responsibility for them.
